title: ESCALATED - Champaign now slipping on branded queries too: page pos 6.0 -> 7.2 (4th straight period), 'forage kitchen champaign' 1.7 -> 3.0, menu variant 1.6 -> 4.0
detail: This is the third week Champaign has been flagged and it has changed character. Clicks to /locations/champaign-il actually ROSE this period (262 -> 298, +14%), which on its own looks fine - but position kept drifting for a fourth consecutive period (4.4 -> 6.1 -> 6.8 -> 7.2) and the drop is now reaching the branded terms that were previously safe: 'forage kitchen champaign' fell from pos 1.7 to 3.0 (still +75 clicks on rising demand, masking the slide) and 'forage kitchen champaign menu' fell from 1.6 to 4.0 with clicks -14. Losing the #1 slot on your own store name is a ranking problem, not demand - the clicks are only holding because Champaign search volume is climbing into the UIUC fall term. If position stays at 3.0 when demand normalizes, the traffic goes with it. Action this week, in order: (1) run a URL inspection on /locations/champaign-il in Search Console - confirm it is indexed, canonical to itself, and last-crawled recently; this is the technical check flagged as the escalation trigger two weeks ago and it is now due. (2) Search 'forage kitchen champaign' from a Champaign IP and record who occupies positions 1-2 - if it is an aggregator (Yelp/DoorDash/Toast page) the fix is internal linking and page authority, not copy. (3) Verify the Champaign Google Business Profile is verified, category 'Restaurant', hours correct through the fall semester, with recent photos and steady review velocity. (4) Add campus/neighborhood terms (UIUC, Campustown, Green Street, downtown Champaign) to the page copy and confirm complete LocalBusiness schema.

title: Sun Prairie is the biggest location decline: -110 clicks (-24%), impressions -2,443, position 2.2 -> 2.6
detail: /locations/sun-prairie fell 460 -> 350 clicks, the largest single-location loss this period and well past the -15% flag threshold, with impressions down 2,443 and position softening 2.2 -> 2.6. Most of this reads as demand rather than lost rankings: the core query 'forage kitchen sun prairie' held position exactly flat at 1.3 while losing 83 clicks, and the menu variant 'forage kitchen sun prairie menu' actually IMPROVED (pos 4.8 -> 3.9). Flat position + falling clicks = fewer people searching, which for a Madison suburb in late summer is a plausible seasonal dip. But the page-level position slip of 0.4 alongside a 2,443-impression drop says the page is also surfacing for fewer discovery queries, so do not write it off entirely. Action: check the Sun Prairie Google Business Profile for anything that suppresses local visibility - hours changed for summer and never restored, a temporary-closure flag, missing/stale photos, or a review-velocity stall vs. the neighboring stores. Compare its GBP against Pewaukee's (which recovered and is now +34 clicks) and match whatever differs. Then confirm the page still carries full LocalBusiness schema with geo coordinates and a menu URL. Re-check next week: if position keeps sliding past 3.0 while clicks fall again, it is a ranking problem and should be treated like Champaign.

title: NEW - '<location> menu' queries losing the #1 slot group-wide, and /menu is down -189 clicks with position 5.3 -> 6.2
detail: A pattern that spans locations, which makes it more actionable than any single page. The main /menu page lost 189 clicks (3,042 -> 2,853) with position falling 5.3 -> 6.2 despite impressions being flat (+457) - stable impressions with worse position and fewer clicks is a ranking slip, not demand. Underneath it, the per-location menu queries moved the same direction: 'forage kitchen whitefish bay menu' 1.8 -> 4.5 (-31 clicks), 'forage kitchen champaign menu' 1.6 -> 4.0 (-14 clicks), 'forage kitchen monona menu' 1.9 -> 4.2. Three different cities dropping from ~pos 1.8 to ~pos 4 in the same period is a site-side change, not three coincidences - something is causing Google to prefer a different URL (or a third-party menu listing) for '<city> menu' intent. Also worth noting 'forage kitchen menu' itself lost 81 clicks even while improving to pos 1.2, so the generic term is fine and the geo-qualified ones are the casualties. Action: (1) Search 'forage kitchen <city> menu' for Whitefish Bay, Champaign and Monona and note which URL now ranks - if it is a DoorDash/Toast/Yelp menu page, that is the competitor to displace. (2) Confirm each /locations/* page links prominently to the menu with anchor text that includes the city ('Whitefish Bay menu', not 'View menu'), and that the location page carries a hasMenu property in its LocalBusiness schema pointing at the menu URL. (3) Check whether a recent site change altered /menu's title tag or its internal links from the location pages. Recovering these three to pos ~2 is worth roughly 60-80 clicks/28d plus whatever /menu regains.

title: Near-me / LocalBusiness schema audit STILL OPEN - 'food near me' improving again (pos 11.9 -> 11.4, +39 clicks) but no progress on the audit itself
detail: Carried forward for a fourth week, unchanged in substance because the audit has not been completed. The trend evidence keeps saying it is worth doing: 'food near me' gained again (127 -> 166 clicks, position improving 11.9 -> 11.4 on 11.3k impressions), which is the strongest signal that Forage can win generic proximity intent. Meanwhile 'healthy food near me' lost 13 clicks with position essentially flat (7.5 -> 7.3), so that one is demand, not ranking. The unfinished work is mechanical and cheap: confirm EVERY /locations/* page carries complete LocalBusiness structured data - name, full postal address, geo latitude/longitude, openingHoursSpecification, telephone, servesCuisine, and a hasMenu URL - plus an embedded Google map. This overlaps directly with the menu-query issue above (hasMenu) and the Champaign and Sun Prairie items, so doing the audit once resolves a piece of three separate flags. Validate with Google's Rich Results Test on two pages (one strong - Whitefish Bay, one weak - State Street) and fix whatever the strong page has that the weak one lacks.

title: Salad content cluster still eroding - /blogs/salad-toppings collapsed 21 -> 1 click (pos 12.2 -> 16.7) and two cobb-salad queries dropped out entirely
detail: Flagged last week as a refresh candidate; it got worse, not better. /blogs/salad-toppings essentially fell off the map (21 -> 1 click, position 12.2 -> 16.7, a 4.5-position drop), and both 'cobb salad calories' (7 clicks, was pos 5.6) and 'is a cobb salad healthy' (4 clicks, was pos 3.3) lost their rankings completely this period. The main post /blogs/cobb-salad-a-healthy-choice is declining more slowly now (-13 clicks, position holding at 5.1 vs 5.0), so the anchor page is stable and the satellite content around it is what is decaying. Also in the same decay pattern: /blogs/caesar-salad -12 clicks (pos 6.8 -> 7.9), /blogs/tepache-101 -10 clicks (pos 7.0 -> 9.1), /menu-items/chicken-chopped-salad -12 clicks with position collapsing 9.4 -> 16.4. Action: pick the two with real recoverable volume - salad-toppings and cobb-salad-a-healthy-choice - and do a genuine refresh, not a date bump: rewrite the intro to match current intent, add a nutrition/calories section (that is the query that was lost), add FAQPage schema answering 'is a cobb salad healthy' and 'how many calories in a cobb salad', and cross-link both from /menu and from each other. Top-of-funnel, so lower urgency than the location and menu items - but it is roughly 80-100 clicks/28d sitting on the table.

title: Healthy quarter overall: clicks +562 (23,554), non-branded +148 (+8.6%), CTR 2.81% -> 3.35% - ignore the -14% impression headline
detail: Context so the top-line numbers are not misread. Impressions fell 819k -> 703k (-14%), and nearly half of that is one page: /blogs/fermented-food shed 47,496 impressions while its position stayed flat (8.6 -> 8.8) and its CLICKS ROSE +57. Stable rank, collapsing impressions, rising clicks is a SERP-feature pullback on a broad informational query (almost certainly an AI overview absorbing the top-of-page), not lost rankings - the same non-issue as the last two weeks. Do not chase it. What matters is that clicks are up (+562), non-branded clicks are up +148 to 1,875 (+8.6%), and CTR improved sharply from 2.81% to 3.35%. Site-wide average position worsened 8.5 -> 9.0, but that is a mix effect from shedding low-ranking informational impressions, not a broad decline. WINS TO BANK: Brookfield is now the standout - /locations/brookfield +100 clicks and 'forage kitchen brookfield' hit pos 1.0 with +310 clicks (the new store's local SEO has fully landed); Pewaukee's recovery held (+34 clicks, pos 3.3); Hilldale's query jumped to pos 1.2 from 3.7; and last week's /faq flag resolved itself - it is out of the loser table and 'forage kitchen nutrition' recovered to +12 clicks. STANDING GAP, unchanged for four weeks: /locations/state-street-madison-wi is still the weakest location page (57 clicks on 6,487 impressions - a 0.9% CTR against 3-4% for its peers) despite strong Madison intent; it is a title/meta-description problem more than a ranking one at pos 4.2. Rewrite its title and description to lead with 'State Street' and 'UW campus' and add a homepage link.
